feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 0 (entityR2B, score 53.612) and iteration 1 (entityR2B, score 53.3955) both ended off_track in all 60 trials, with max_error at 0.061 to 0.066 m, 1 to 2 line-loss events, and steering_oscillation of 0.07 to 0.16. Moving from 10 mm to 15 mm pitch did not reduce line losses or max_error, so sensor pitch is not the only limit. Narrowing the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m also did not improve max_error (oval 0.0608 to 0.0621), so track narrowing is not an effective steering lever. For this candidate I widen the bar to 20 mm pitch and keep the footprint at 12 mm, and I raise kp in the controller to test steering authority. Next race: if line_loss_events drop to 0 and max_error stays near 0.06 m, the limit is lag or steering rather than coverage, so move the forward offset to y = 0.06 m to give the sensors more lead. If line_loss_events still reach 1 or more, the 12 mm footprint is too small for the 25 mm tape at the outer sensors, so try sensor_size 0.016 with the same 20 mm pitch. If line losses are gone and progress is still low with off_track endings, do not narrow the track further, since that did not help max_error.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is still 1 or more with the 20 mm pitch, try sensor_size 0.016 at the same x positions (-0.04 to +0.04, y = 0.04). Evidence: 15 mm pitch in iteration 1 still gave 1 line loss per run, and the 12 mm footprint may be too small at the outer sensors.

If line_loss_events reach 0 and max_error stays near 0.06 m, move the sensor bar forward to y = 0.06 m to add lead and earlier correction. Evidence: iteration 1 showed steady drift (oscillation 0.07 to 0.16) with no max_error gain from track narrowing, so the limit looks like lag rather than coverage.
Do not narrow wheel_track below 0.10 m. Evidence: iteration 1 narrowed the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m and max_error did not improve (oval 0.0608 to 0.0621).
